I am seventy years old, and I have farmed the land in Quzhou County since I was a boy. My father taught me, and I only finished primary school, but I know the soil and weather here better than any book. I have about five mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. At my age, I do not try new things that might fail. I stick to what has fed my family for decades: winter wheat followed by summer maize.

Every October, I rotary-till the field and sow improved wheat seed—usually something like Jimai 22 or Luyuan 502 that the seed station sells. I put down compound fertilizer as a basal dressing, then topdress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring. The wheat needs four irrigations: winter water, green-up water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I spray insecticide twice, herbicide once, and fungicide once. I harvest in early June.

Right after the wheat comes off, I plant hybrid maize—Denghai 605 or similar—using no-tillage. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at sowing. Maize grows fast in the summer heat and only needs two irrigations. I spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. I harvest in September or October, then the cycle starts again.

The government buys wheat at a guaranteed price, so that is my safe crop. Maize brings cash and feeds my family. I do not grow cotton anymore—it needs too much labor for an old man. Vegetables are risky; prices go up and down too much. This rotation is simple, and it works.
